lxc_3b62c6adfb8bce34.text: You are choosing a drink and dessert with Leo at the imaginary cafe, which serves cold tea and slices of cake.

lxc_160b98b05c992257.text: You want a small cold tea without sugar and a slice of cake to enjoy there.

lxc_94846b6a33140443.text: A cold tea without sugar, please.

lxc_321463bea671cf94.text: A cafe order can start with a drink and something sweet.

lxc_039819ad8d952c6a.text: In our imaginary cafe, Maya serves hot coffee and cold tea.

lxc_7a43f4e48631ee67.text: Coffee can come with milk, while the cold tea can come without sugar.

lxc_1ffd7f137e0c0236.text: These details matter because two people can order tea but want different drinks.

lxc_e0003ec6f2f844c1.text: A small cup holds less than a large cup.

lxc_c28589a910403e7a.text: Maya also serves cake by the slice and cookies as separate pieces.

lxc_db07f819b4231b94.text: A slice of cake and a cookie are two different dessert choices.

lxc_c8a5e24a02d37343.text: One person might want only a drink, while another wants both.

lxc_95e785a7939ccd39.text: The drink, its size, and the dessert are separate parts of the order.

lxc_1369c3a14efa0361.text: Clear details help Maya prepare the right things.

lxc_44080cfb4458ef8d.text: You are ordering a hot drink from Maya at the imaginary cafe counter, where coffee comes in small and large cups.

lxc_f5df29527cf3ed1b.text: You want a small hot coffee with milk to take away.

lxc_dba4de680ce0a28e.text: Your goal is to order the drink and confirm its size.

lxc_d26731597117e962.text: Cafe orders bring together drinks, desserts, and ways to pay.

lxc_8c40b54b4d1ddeed.text: The cafe situations here are imaginary.

lxc_157e7a7622c5aaf6.text: A clear order helps the person serving you understand what you want.

lxc_8bd2c75bf2ffd029.text: An order is easier to follow when its details stay together.

lxc_94b19ccb626649fa.text: The drink name tells the cafe worker what to prepare.

lxc_680f7eea12501703.text: Words such as small, hot, and cold make that choice clearer.

lxc_40f802b54c7d8a6a.text: In our imaginary cafe, Leo takes an order for a small hot coffee with milk.

lxc_fa67b6ead9a4ec03.text: He repeats the drink details before preparing it.

lxc_81a6cc990344f016.text: The customer listens and confirms that the order is right.

lxc_7f3d2386c80bea76.text: A dessert can follow as another part of the same order.

lxc_b5ed420733645cb9.text: Leo then adds a cookie for this customer.

lxc_4d43df5674f2e3c9.text: An order can also include whether the customer will stay or take it away.

lxc_69d2728c28e9f238.text: This customer will stay, so Leo now has the complete order.

lxc_714868534545389b.text: Payment comes after the order is clear in these imaginary cafe situations.

lxc_c982bc604f1a81dd.text: Here, Maya accepts both card and cash, but that is a detail of this story, not a rule for every cafe.

lxc_cdf7df87a6125a11.text: A customer chooses how to pay before Maya finishes the sale.

lxc_03b3c11d04806ba6.text: With cash, the customer gives money directly to Maya.

lxc_56f91b543186a9e0.text: With a card, the customer uses the card machine.

lxc_9207ca6247f803b1.text: The bill should match the food and drinks the customer ordered.

lxc_18fdc49f1f7227a9.text: In this example, Maya notices an extra cookie on the bill.

lxc_b597f8190fdb940b.text: She removes it before taking payment.

lxc_806cf7d286d09585.text: The customer then pays by card and gets a receipt.

lxc_6c74d2dfab7eb1a6.text: Fixing the order first keeps the payment clear for both people.
